# Results — Study 609 (VIX Weekend Arithmetic)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the VIX
has a guaranteed day-of-week seesaw baked into its own formula: pure calendar-variance
arithmetic (30 calendar days in the window, variance accruing mostly on trading days) drifts
the index down into the weekend and pops it back on Monday** — tested on the full ^VIX history
(1990+). One important correction up front: the popular retelling often quotes the sign
**backwards** ("VIX drifts up into Friday, drops on Monday"); the arithmetic unambiguously
predicts the **opposite** — down into Thursday/Friday as the weekend enters the 30-day window,
up on Monday once it has passed — and that is exactly what the tape shows. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (last complete month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints
`63115cff08dc` (^VIX) / `829eafeefcc4` (VIXY).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance **^VIX** daily closes (public, no key) — 9,191 rows, 1990-01-02 → 2026-06-30; **9,190** close-to-close log changes |
| Third-axis tape | yfinance **VIXY** auto-adjusted (total-return) daily closes — 3,894 rows, 2011-01-04 → 2026-06-30 (**15.5** years, 728 weekends) |
| Survivorship | none on the Signal axis — ^VIX is a single continuously published index, not a survivor panel; VIXY is the surviving continuous-tape short-term VIX-futures ETP (named on the third axis) |
| Units | daily change of ln(VIX) in **%** (the natural unit for a level that ranges 9→83) |
| Execution / costs (third axis) | the weekday calendar is known in advance, so entry at **Friday's close** is the one documented execution lag (no look-ahead by construction); one round trip per weekend at **2 / 5 / 10 bps** one-way |

## The signal — the day-of-week table

Mean daily change of ln(VIX) by the weekday the close lands on, 1990-01-03 → 2026-06-30:

| weekday | mean Δln VIX | one-sample *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Monday** | **+1.805 %/day** | **+10.25** | 1,733 |
| Tuesday | −0.158 %/day | −1.05 | 1,886 |
| Wednesday | −0.564 %/day | −3.82 | 1,883 |
| Thursday | +0.013 %/day | +0.09 | 1,849 |
| **Friday** | **−0.977 %/day** | **−6.02** | 1,839 |

**The headline contrast — Monday vs Friday:**

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| Mon − Fri spread | **+2.783 %/day** |
| Welch *t* | **+11.61** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* (dummy-regression contrast) | **+11.19** |
| HAC *t* vs mid-week base: Monday / Friday | +10.23 / −3.96 |
| label-shuffle placebo (20,000 draws) | **p < 1/20,000** (no draw reached the observed spread) |

The seesaw is enormous by calendar-anomaly standards — a **+2.8 %/day** Monday-minus-Friday
spread at HAC *t* ≈ 11 on 36.5 years of tape. It clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar by a factor of
five, and its direction is **down into Friday, up on Monday** — the sign the arithmetic
predicts, and the opposite of the "up into Friday" folk version.

## The arithmetic race — how much of it is the day-count model?

Model: the VIX squares to 30-**calendar**-day expected variance, but variance accrues mostly on
**trading** days. If a weekend day carries a fraction *f* of a trading day's variance, the
quoted index is ∝ √(N_eff/30) with N_eff = trading days + *f* × weekend days in the window —
and the window's day counts depend on the quote day: Mon/Tue/Wed = (22, 8), Thu = (21, 9),
**Fri = (20, 10)**. Predicted change on weekday *d* = 50·ln(N_eff(d)/N_eff(d−1)) percent.

| weekday | full arithmetic (*f* = 0) | observed | model at fitted *f* = 0.597 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Mon | +4.77 % | **+1.81 %** | +1.53 % |
| Tue | +0.00 % | −0.16 % | +0.00 % |
| Wed | +0.00 % | −0.56 % | +0.00 % |
| Thu | −2.33 % | +0.01 % | −0.76 % |
| Fri | −2.44 % | **−0.98 %** | −0.77 % |

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| implied weekend fraction *f* (least squares over the 5 weekday means) | **0.597** |
| fit RMSE | 0.46 %/day |

The tape shows the model's **shape** (pop on Monday, mark-down concentrated at the end of the
week) at roughly **40 % of the full-arithmetic amplitude**: the market prices a weekend day at
**~60 % of a trading day's variance**, not zero. So the seesaw is *not* "pure" arithmetic in the
zero-weekend-variance sense — it is the arithmetic **times the market's partial weekend
discount**. The fit is imperfect in the details (the tape puts more of the mark-down on
Wednesday and less on Thursday than the stylized model), which is why *f* is a summary, not a law.

## Robustness — every decade, and holidays too

| decade | Mon mean | Fri mean | spread | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1990–1999 | +2.345 % | −1.120 % | +3.464 % | **+8.77** |
| 2000–2009 | +1.856 % | −0.593 % | +2.449 % | **+6.63** |
| 2010–2019 | +1.565 % | −1.217 % | +2.781 % | **+5.20** |
| 2020–2026 | +1.247 % | −0.981 % | +2.229 % | **+3.34** |

The spread has narrowed by roughly a third since the 1990s but clears *t* = 2 in **every**
decade — as a mechanical effect should. Cutting by **calendar gap** instead of weekday label
(which also catches holiday weekends): post-gap days (previous close ≥ 3 calendar days back)
average **+2.067 %/day** (n = 1,904) vs **−0.997 %/day** on pre-gap days (n = 1,904) and
−0.379 %/day mid-week — post-vs-pre Welch *t* = **+13.21**, post-vs-mid *t* = **+12.83**. The
effect follows market closures, not the "Monday" label — the mechanism's signature.

## Third axis — can a VIX-futures ETP harvest the Monday pop?

The index is not tradable; the accessible vehicle is a short-term VIX-futures ETP (VIXY, the
continuous-tape VXX-equivalent, total-return, 2011+). The trade: **buy VIXY at Friday's close,
sell at Monday's close** — the calendar is known in advance, so the Friday-close entry is the
single documented execution lag.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| ^VIX index Monday mean (matched 2011–2026 window) | **+1.626 %** |
| **VIXY Monday (over-weekend) mean** | **−0.324 %** (one-sample *t* = −1.72) |
| VIXY other-day mean | −0.136 %/day |
| Monday-vs-rest Welch *t* | −0.92 |
| weekends / cadence | 728 over 15.5 years (~47 trades/yr) |
| weekend-hold P&L, gross | **−15.2 %/yr** |
| net at 2 / 5 / 10 bps one-way | **−17.1 % / −19.9 % / −24.6 %/yr** |

The pop does **not** leak. While the index jumps +1.63 % on the average Monday, the ETP —
priced off futures that **anticipate** the arithmetic — *loses* 0.32 % over the same weekend
(if anything more than its usual daily roll bleed, and in the **wrong direction** for the
harvest; Welch *t* = −0.92, indistinguishable from its ordinary decay). The weekend-hold
strategy loses ~15 %/yr before costs and ~20 %/yr after. There is nothing to harvest: the
seesaw lives in the index's *formula*, and every tradable claim on the VIX is priced by people
who own calendars.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic log-AR(1) "true vol", quoted through the day-count arithmetic with a **planted**
weekend fraction *f* (*f* = 1.0 ⇒ weekends count fully ⇒ no weekday pattern = the null):

| planted *f* | Mon−Fri spread | Welch *t* | NW *t* | recovered *f* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1.0 (null)** | −0.111 % | −0.63 | −0.64 | 1.000 |
| **0.3 (planted)** | +4.342 % | +24.49 | +25.09 | **0.308** |

With no planted effect the machinery sits at *t* ≈ −0.6 and correctly reports *f* = 1; with a
planted *f* = 0.3 it lights up and recovers *f* = 0.308. The estimator is unbiased in both
directions. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape
stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The VIX weekend seesaw is one of the largest, most stable calendar
  patterns on any tape the desk has run: Monday **+1.81 %/day**, Friday **−0.98 %/day**,
  Mon−Fri spread **+2.78 %/day** at Welch *t* = **11.6** / Newey-West *t* = **11.2**, placebo
  p < 1/20,000, *t* ≥ 3.3 in every decade, and it tracks calendar gaps (holidays included) at
  *t* = 13.2. Direction exactly as the variance-day-count arithmetic predicts — and **opposite**
  to the "drifts up into Friday" folk retelling. Magnitude ≈ 40 % of the full-arithmetic bound:
  the market prices a weekend day at ~**60 %** of a trading day's variance, so it is the
  arithmetic × a partial weekend discount, not "pure" arithmetic.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The index itself is not tradable, and the pop does not leak into
  the tradable claim: VIXY's over-weekend return is **−0.32 %** (the wrong direction) while the
  index jumps +1.63 %; the literal Friday-close→Monday-close harvest loses **−15 %/yr gross**
  and **−20 %/yr net** at 5 bps. Futures are priced off the *forward* VIX by people who can
  count weekends.
- **"Can a VIX ETP harvest the Monday pop?" — BUSTED.** 728 weekends, 15.5 years: Monday-vs-rest
  Welch *t* = −0.92 and a negative mean. The seesaw is a property of the index's formula, fully
  anticipated in every instrument you can actually buy.
